plain_text:
There are more than 80 known autoimmune conditions,
which together affect more than 23,5 million Americans.
Each disease is different, but what they all have in common
is a haywire immune response that turns the immune
system against the body it is supposed to protect.
semantic_text: There are more than 80 known autoimmune conditions, which together affect more than 23,5 million Americans. Each disease is different, but what they all have in common is a haywire immune response that turns the immune system against the body it is supposed to protect.

plain_text:
Some conditions target specific organs or tissues,
such as the skin, heart, or blood vessels. Others are more
general, targeting multiple tissue or organ systems
throughout the body.
semantic_text: Some conditions target specific organs or tissues, such as the skin, heart, or blood vessels. Others are more general, targeting multiple tissue or organ systems throughout the body.

plain_text:
Examples of common organ-specific conditions include
type 1 diabetes (pancreas), inflammatory bowel diseases
such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis (digestive tract),
and multiple sclerosis (brain and spinal cord).
semantic_text: Examples of common organ-specific conditions include type 1 diabetes (pancreas), inflammatory bowel diseases such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis (digestive tract), and multiple sclerosis (brain and spinal cord).

plain_text:
Systemic conditions—those that attack multiple
systems—include systemic lupus erythematosus,
also known as lupus or SLE, Sjögren's syndrome,
and scleroderma, which all affect tissues and organs
throughout the body.
semantic_text: Systemic conditions—those that attack multiple systems—include systemic lupus erythematosus, also known as lupus or SLE, Sjögren's syndrome, and scleroderma, which all affect tissues and organs throughout the body.

plain_text:
While scientists and doctors aren't exactly sure what
causes autoimmune diseases, they are likely triggered
by interactions between genes, the immune system,
and the environment.
semantic_text: While scientists and doctors aren't exactly sure what causes autoimmune diseases, they are likely triggered by interactions between genes, the immune system, and the environment.

plain_text:
There's still a lot to learn about these relationships,
but experts think that even if a person with certain
genes or certain combinations of genes is at risk of
an autoimmune disease, they probably won't develop
the condition without something in their environment
triggering it or turning it on. Environmental triggers
may include:
semantic_text: There's still a lot to learn about these relationships, but experts think that even if a person with certain genes or certain combinations of genes is at risk of an autoimmune disease, they probably won't develop the condition without something in their environment triggering it or turning it on. Environmental triggers may include:

plain_text:
■ Infection (from a virus or bacteria)
■ Stress
■ Dietary components (such as gluten or dairy)
■ Contaminants in food (such as mercury in fish)
■ Environmental pollutants (such as certain pesticides)
semantic_text: ■ Infection (from a virus or bacteria) ■ Stress ■ Dietary components (such as gluten or dairy) ■ Contaminants in food (such as mercury in fish) ■ Environmental pollutants (such as certain pesticides)

plain_text:
Autoimmune diseases tend to run in families. You're more
likely to develop one if you:
semantic_text: Autoimmune diseases tend to run in families. You're more likely to develop one if you:

plain_text:
■ Have a family member with an autoimmune disease
■ Are already diagnosed with one or more autoimmune
diseases
semantic_text: ■ Have a family member with an autoimmune disease ■ Are already diagnosed with one or more autoimmune diseases

plain_text:
Also, your racial and ethnic background, assigned sex,
and age may make you more or less likely to develop
certain autoimmune diseases. For example, many kinds
of autoimmune diseases such as lupus, scleroderma, and
Sjögren's syndrome are far more common among women
than among men.
semantic_text: Also, your racial and ethnic background, assigned sex, and age may make you more or less likely to develop certain autoimmune diseases. For example, many kinds of autoimmune diseases such as lupus, scleroderma, and Sjögren's syndrome are far more common among women than among men.

plain_text:
Because specific viruses or environmental conditions

may trigger autoimmune diseases, the risk of certain
autoimmune diseases may be higher in people who are
more likely to be exposed to those triggers.
semantic_text:
